category: AI System Design, Production Serving & LLMOps

content.tldr: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search across past prompt embeddings to return cached responses for semantically identical questions, cutting API latency and billing costs.
content.simple_explanation: Traditional web caches (like Redis) perform exact string key lookups, which fail on AI prompts because users phrase identical questions differently ('How do I reset my password?' vs 'Where can I change my login password?'). A semantic cache embeds incoming user prompts and searches a vector database of prior queries. If the cosine similarity exceeds a configured threshold (such as 0.92), the cached response is served immediately with sub-50ms latency without invoking the expensive LLM backend.
content.real_world_example: A customer service helpdesk: instead of escalating every customer who asks how to track a package to a live agent, a smart triage system recognizes equivalent phrasing and supplies the standard tracking guide.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Setting similarity thresholds too loosely causes catastrophic semantic drift, returning answers to queries with opposing intent ('How to enable 2FA' vs 'How to disable 2FA'). High-risk enterprise domains must scope cache keys by user tenant and role permissions.
